tissue Na content is increased in several organ systems of patients at risk for or suffering from cardiovascular and renal diseases.

the development and validation of Na-MRI and its application to elucidate the role of tissue Na content for the understanding of cardiovascular diseases.
the development of Na-MRI and its application to investigate Na storage in patients with cardiovascular diseases and related organ damage.
the role of Na accumulation in the pathogenesis of organ damage and the development of a novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategy.

tissue Na content may serve as a novel biomarker of organ damage.

tissue Na content can be used as a noninvasive and reliable biomarker to identify patients at risk for cardiovascular complications.

tissue Na content is an independent marker for organ damage in patients with risk factors such as hypertension, diabetes mellitus, heart failure and chronic kidney disease.

tissue Na content is a new, non-invasive, reliable biomarker of organ damage.
